headline: How a Grade 1 star got her start

before_slider.lead: In South Africa, fewer than half of children in early learning programs are on track to start school ready to learn.

before_slider.p: Our partner True North is working to change that in Vrygrond, one of Cape Town’s poorest neighborhoods, and a busy, bustling one. It trains, mentors and equips 30 preschools and 144 staff, who care for more than 1,700 young children each day. Melokuhle is one of the children who started school ready.

She is seven and lives with her mom, Anna, who works as a security guard. This January, she started Grade 1. She does math and words in Afrikaans and English, and her report is already full of sevens, the top mark in South Africa’s early grades.

That didn’t happen by accident. Melokuhle spent two years at Rainbow Educare ECD, a True North-supported preschool, from the age of four. When she arrived, she was quiet and held back. What she needed most, says principal Faranaaz Jacobs, was “positive affirmation,” and her teachers gave it to her, again and again.

There, she learned through play. She loved story time, then drew pictures of everything she’d heard. She became the class helper, and was often the first to finish her work. “That was when we realized that she found a safe space,” Faranaaz says.

after_slider.p: Ask Melokuhle about preschool, and she remembers the bikes, the balls and the big plastic playhouse outside, playing hide-and-seek with her friends, and teachers who were kind. She was happy, and wanted to go to school every day.

Faranaaz has seen this for 28 years, since she founded Rainbow Educare. A child who has been to a good preschool, she says, “will then be able to stand out… you can clearly see that the child is developed in all his learning areas.”
Her mom sees it too. “Melo is very good for school, for everything,” says Anna. “Even teacher come to me say Melo is very, very, very good.”
after_slider.flag: Open with Clem (STORY.md §4): adds "is" to the transcript's line; kept as she wrote it

after_slider.display: One preschool. A whole community of children.

after_slider.p: Rainbow Educare is one of 30 preschools True North supports in Vrygrond. It trains teachers in play-based learning, mentors principals like Faranaaz on running a strong center, and helps preschools earn the equipment children need. Rainbow Educare has now reached red status, the highest mark on True North’s development framework. Even Ground has supported True North since 2019.
“Early learning literally shapes the architecture of the brain,” says Faranaaz.
Donations to Even Ground help fund community-centered programs like True North’s, so more children like Melokuhle can start school ready to learn.
